title: Understanding PCA and SVD
text: PCA (Principal Component Analysis) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It uses SVD (Singular Value Decomposition) to decompose the data matrix into three matrices: U, S, and $$V^T$$. The matrix S contains the singular values, which are crucial for determining the principal components.

title: Properties of V Matrix
text: The matrix V in SVD is an orthogonal matrix, meaning its columns are orthonormal vectors. This means each column vector has a norm of $$1$$, and the dot product between any two different columns is $$0$$.
